title: Herringbone htr — the pull-through shortcut
subtitle: Draw through all the loops at once instead of separately — flatter, denser, faster
excerpt: Herringbone htr pulls the working yarn through two loops at once on the first draw-through instead of stopping at the usual three-loop htr stage. The result is a flatter, tighter-looking half treble that tiles into a herringbone V-pattern across the fabric. It works up faster and produces a denser, less holey fabric than standard htr.

glossaryTerms.definition: A half treble variant where the initial yarn-over draw-through pulls through both the loop on the hook AND the yarn-over in one motion, leaving 2 loops. Then yarn over, draw through both. The stitch leans slightly and creates a herringbone V-diagonal texture across the fabric.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: The pull-through step: drawing yarn through both the loop and the yarn-over in one go, leaving just 2 loops on hook

content.text: modifies the standard htr sequence at the first draw-through step. In a normal htr, you yarn over, insert, draw up a loop (3 loops on hook), then yarn over and draw through all 3. In herringbone htr, that first draw-through goes through the loop on the hook AND the yarn-over simultaneously — skipping straight from 3 loops down to 2 in one motion. The stitch sits flatter against the fabric and the diagonal of each stitch creates the herringbone pattern.
Yarn over. Insert the hook into the next stitch.
Yarn over and draw through both the stitch AND the first loop already on the hook in one pull — 2 loops remain on hook. This is the key difference from standard htr.
Yarn over and draw through both remaining loops. One herringbone htr made.
Continue across the row. The stitches lean slightly and align into a V-diagonal pattern.

items.symptom: Stitch comes out the same as standard htr
items.cause: Drawing through only the stitch on the first pull, not through the stitch plus the yarn-over
items.fix: On step 2, the hook must push through the stitch entrance and pull the yarn through both the stitch AND the yarn-over that's waiting on the hook in one continuous draw. Practice slowly until the motion becomes distinct from the normal htr.

content.text: Herringbone dc and herringbone tr follow the same principle — the pull-through-two trick applied to dc and treble. Each height produces a different scale of herringbone V texture.
